speaker: SPEAKER_01
transcript: In some ways, it's been very rewarding. In other ways, it's been incredibly frustrating. I was able to get the Dairy Business Innovation Act through which I thought is great. That's going to help increase funding to a program that allows our dairy men and women to explore different ways to market their products. And I think we got to keep doing that. I was one of eight people that stood up to the entire Republican establishment and said, we are not going to vote for this limit-save growth. or the Fiscal Responsibility Act until you put back in our provisions for biofuels, sustainable aviation fuels, carbons, sequestration stuff, nuclear power, biodiesel, tax credits for our co-ops. The majority folks get their power from rural co-ops here in the third. And, you know, they just kind of forgot about us people in little old Wisconsin. So we said, no, we're not doing it. And all those got put back in, which was a big deal because I'm a freshman. And I just got a letter cranked off to Canada, to the United States government, and the Canadian government about how Canada's jamminess and USMCA again, they're not holding up their part of the bargain, and our dairy men are getting shafted for that. We got the whole milk for Healthy Kids Act through. In 2010, when Michelle Obama was the first lady, she decided that whole milk and 2% milk was bad for you, and they pulled it out of all the schools. And that's why kids stopped drinking milk. And if you drink skim milk, that's fine. I personally believe it tastes a little bit like chalk water myself. I'm a whole milk kind of guy. And we got that past so that the children will have a choice to drink 2% milk and whole milk and chocolate milk in schools again. And I think that is fantastic. We got Dairy Farm Resilency Act, which is going to help the dairy margin costs program. We got to get it. That has to be worked out. And so we're working diligently on that. And then I'm really happy about getting $2 million for the township of Campbell and also for the city of Eau Claire to help treat their water for PFAS. That's those forever chemicals that were mandated by the federal government that you use it or that the fire departments on airfields use it to fight aircraft fuel. So it's 2023 in the United States of America and you should be able to drink clean water out of your own tap. So we've been very busy this year.
